Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Putting a short acceptance probe together below and attaching a few starter artifacts. TL;DR: we support both proxy-forwarding (customer-controlled outbound) and a strict allowlist; we recommend running the probe window with a proxy in front first, then switch to an allowlist once NAT/eBPF rules are validated.

Quick checklist (high level):
- Control plane endpoints (required): control.redwood.ai (443), config.redwood.ai (443) — prefer FQDN + TLS SNI allowlist rather than wide IP ranges.
- Artifact fetches (model and weights): model-cdn.redwood.ai (443). We publish signed digests; downloads can be proxied through your internal gateway.
- Telemetry & health pings (optional but recommended): telemetry.redwood.ai (443). These can be disabled; note that disabling will limit RL/auto-healing telemetry.
- Port and protocol: outbound TCP 443 only. No inbound required.
- Evidence/artifacts: sample allowlist CSV, a YAML snippet showing agent outbound config, and a brief POAM summary (attached).

Attachments included: private-endpoint-sample-config.yaml, egress-allowlist-template.csv, poam-scan-summary.pdf

Audit pack ETA: simple evidence (allowlist + signed runbook excerpt) — ~2 business days; fuller bundle (TLS fingerprints, packet captures, signed manifest of model digests) — 5–7 business days. We’ll work with you on what to include.

Next steps:
1) Do you want us to run the initial probe from our side (we can initiate test connections and return a report), or do you prefer to run in your staging environment?
2) If you prefer to proxy, can you share the proxy hostname and whether it supports mTLS client certs?

Looping in David (runtime networking) and Marissa (compliance) to confirm the artifacts and timeline.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samir — thank you for the patience. Quick summary and proposed timeline after internal check-ins: 

What we will provide (concise deliverables):
- A one-page acceptance checklist (what to open/verify) — attached as CSV and YAML snippets.
- A 2-business-day evidence bundle that contains: allowlist CSV, signed manifest of agent artifact digests, sample packet-capture of a successful TLS handshake (redacted), and a short explanatory runbook PDF.
- If you want the fuller audit pack (TLS fingerprints + extended logs): 5 business days.

Network specifics (minimal posture):
- Outbound TCP 443 to the following FQDNs: control.redwood.ai, config.redwood.ai, model-cdn.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai. We recommend SNI-based allowlisting; if auditors require IPs we can supply a short-lived NAT IP set updated daily (ephemeral NAT) and a signed attest that those are the only egress IPs used during the probe window.
- No inbound ports required.
- Optional: proxy with mTLS. If you can terminate mTLS at your gateway, agent supports client cert presentation. If you prefer Redwood-managed cert exchange, Kimberly will send the cert workflow doc.

Proposed schedule:
- 2025-10-15: Customer staging window — you run a proxy-forwarded probe and provide proxy FQDN + sample ACL (if you want Redwood to run tests we will need proxy login details or a staging NAT IP to reach).
- 2025-10-17: Redwood returns 2-day evidence bundle and a short report indicating success/fail per check.

Action items for Samir:
- Reply with preference: (A) run probe from your staging (recommended), or (B) have Redwood initiate tests from our integration lab.
- If (A): provide proxy hostname and confirm whether mTLS is required.

I’ll have the attached artifacts and a short statement about telemetry opt-out ready when you confirm. Looping Kimberly to send the cert-exchange doc and Marissa to sign off on the 2-day evidence contents.
